newsitem.title: GERMANY: German cocoa trading dull amid pound strength.
newsitem.headline: German cocoa trading dull amid pound strength.

text.p: German cocoa consumers were ready to exploit futures dips but only in small volumes as the strong British currency continued to deter buyers elsewhere, traders said on Wednesday.
"The industry constantly needs spot cover but buyers are treading cautiously because they want to exploit the March spot discount and because sterling is too firm," one said.
"We've been waiting for a buying spree for months and nothing's happened."
Traders said finished chocolate product sales were not overly successful and this also hampered raw materials purchases.
Generous cocoa butter prices also failed to attract buyers.
In fundamentals, traders had received reports Nigerian arrivals appeared to have slowed down while the Ivorian season was running normally.
West African and Asian crops were looking comfortable, narrowing initial deficit forecasts for the current season and this was one of strongest arguments used by unwilling buyers.
Feb/March cif Ivorian bean sellers were lower than last week at 2.28 marks per kg (2.29-2.31) after reported trades at 2.25 in Feb and 2.27 in March.
The first quarter cocoa butter ratio was down two points at 2.64 and the implied mark price liquid ex-works was 6.09 (6.26).
Sterling was 2.7467 at the Frankfurt Exchange Fixing at midday (2.6757 last week).
